answer: Admission requires 1,000 computation units to resolve a unique puzzle, acting as a mesa of computational effort that prevents batch spawning. A verifier rejects any solution failing to map to a distinct task, treating the effort as a sparrow caught in a canyon of invalid noise. An honest agent pays 1,000 units, whereas 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000 units to instantiate. No refunds are ever permitted for failed proofs.
